A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable main text, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–G. Displays can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 surveys existing benchmarks and methods. Its experimental findings are attributed to cited studies; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature survey. Its revised tables, additional citations, and research directions introduce no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Neither version introduces an original algorithm or model. The procedures reviewed in Section 4 and Appendix F remain unchanged; edits to their comparison table do not establish method changes.

E1.justification: The same text-only, multimodal household, and interactive game benchmarks remain covered in Section 3 and Appendices C–E. New research suggestions do not introduce datasets or scenarios actually used for evaluation.

E2.justification: The reviewed comparison methods remain the same, including SYMBOLICTOM, SIMTOM, PercepToM, TIMETOM, ToM-LM, BIP-ALM, and LIMP. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: LIMP's reported testing depth changes from 'tested up to third-order' in v1 Table 3 to 'up to second-order' in v2 Table 2. This revises the documented evaluation scope of a cited study; it does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Neither version adds or removes ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical error analyses. The worked prompting example and discussions of pipeline errors and perception limitations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run information, uncertainty intervals, significance tests, or other statistical reporting procedures.

E6.justification: The empirical outcome summaries remain unchanged, including LIMP outperforming BIP-ALM on MuMA-ToM. No performance scores or measured outcomes are added or revised; the LIMP reasoning-order correction concerns reported test scope.

T1.justification: The ToM concepts in Section 2 and the perception, recency, and reciprocity assumptions in Appendix F retain their meaning. Neither version adds or revises formal mathematical results, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a broad survey of ToM assessment and enhancement, analysis of benchmark and method development, and identification of future directions. The rewritten abstract and introduction retain this scope and novelty claim; the conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.1.2 recasts question evolution from multiple-choice versus open-ended formats to single versus multiple question-answering tasks. Section 5 adds probing internal mental-state representations, and Appendix G adds multi-party negotiations as motivation for higher-order reasoning. The dedicated Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Footnote 2 corrects the GPT-4 documentation link's truncated destination from '/models/gp' to '/models/gpt-4'. This is a limited resource-reference correction; no implementation settings, hardware details, or code/data releases are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bortoletto et al. (2024a) on limitations in collaborative dialogue and Bortoletto et al. (2024b) on mental-state representations. The survey's research positioning remains stable. MuMA-ToM's change from a 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 publication is a bibliographic update.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, condenses the NegotiationToM description and future-directions prose, and edits terminology and references. Affiliations are updated and acknowledgments added, while the main section and appendix structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Three central displays move from appendix pages into the main discussion: Table 1, the methods table (v1 Table 3 becomes v2 Table 2), and the prompting diagram (Figure 3 becomes Figure 2). Table 1 gains row separators, and the methods table is compacted around 'Order Tested'. This substantially reorganizes access to the comparisons while largely reusing existing content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves usability by placing key comparisons beside their main-text discussion. Its revised LIMP entry now agrees with the retained description of MuMA-ToM's second-order scope, and the internal-representation research direction modestly enriches the survey. These are useful, limited gains; the central coverage, method analysis, and conclusions remain substantially unchanged.
